title: Data Interception During Registration
description: Sensitive registration data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) transmitted in transit could be intercepted by third parties, enabling linkability of the parent user's identity across systems.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard TLS encryption is not guaranteed; if implemented, likelihood reduces.

title: Metadata Linkability in Transit
description: Metadata about the data flow (timing, volume, source/destination) could be used to identify or link the parent user's registration activity to other data sources.
uncertainty_note: Depends on network monitoring capabilities and metadata exposure.

title: Unauthorized Data Storage at Authentication Service
description: The Authentication Service (P1) may store sensitive registration data (especially government ID and password) without adequate access controls, leading to unauthorized disclosure.
uncertainty_note: Assumes standard security practices may not be fully implemented.

title: Identity Usurpation via Credential Compromise
description: If registration credentials (password, six-digit code) are compromised at the destination, attackers could usurp the parent user's identity and access the authentication service.
uncertainty_note: Depends on password strength, code delivery mechanism, and service security.

title: User Identification via Sensitive Data Sharing
description: The parent user (EE1) shares highly identifiable information (government ID, name, email) which directly enables identification of the individual.
uncertainty_note: This is inherent to the registration process; severity depends on data minimization practices.

title: Non-repudiation of Registration Data Submission
description: The parent user may later deny submitting certain registration data (e.g., government ID, six-digit code), creating disputes about data authenticity and consent.
uncertainty_note: Likelihood depends on user awareness and legal context.

title: Data Interception in Transit
description: Parent account data transmitted from Authentication Service to MongoDB users collection could be intercepted during transit if not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without adequate encryption
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard network transmission without explicit encryption controls documented

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure at Storage
description: MongoDB users collection storing parent account data may expose personal information to unauthorized access if access controls are insufficient.
assumptions: MongoDB instance has potential access by unauthorized parties
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard MongoDB deployment without explicit access control documentation

title: Denial of Confidentiality at Storage
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB may become available to unauthorized parties if database security measures are inadequate.
assumptions: Database lacks proper access controls and encryption at rest
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard MongoDB deployment without explicit security documentation

title: Identification via JWT Token Transmission
description: JWT tokens transmitted in the data flow contain user identifiers that can be used to identify the parent user to external observers or attackers intercepting the communication.

title: Linkability of User Requests via JWT
description: JWT tokens enable linking of multiple requests to the same user, allowing correlation of user activities across different system interactions.

title: Data Disclosure in Transit
description: User data transmitted over the data flow may be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information.

title: Usurpation via JWT Token Sharing
description: The authentication service shares JWT tokens that could be stolen or misused by attackers to impersonate the legitimate parent user.

title: Identification at Destination
description: The parent user receives user data that may contain personally identifiable information, creating identification risks at the destination.

title: Parent email enables account linking
description: The parent email address transmitted during child login can be used to link the child's account to the parent's identity, potentially revealing family relationships and enabling correlation across systems.
assumptions: Parent email is unique and not anonymized; external systems may have access to parent email data.

title: Child identity revealed through parent email
description: By sharing parent email during login, the child user's identity becomes indirectly identifiable through the parent's email address, which may be publicly associated with the parent.
assumptions: Parent email is not anonymized and may be publicly available or indexed.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of authentication credentials
description: The authentication service receives and processes parent email and password data. Inadequate access controls or logging could lead to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive authentication information.
assumptions: Authentication service may have insufficient access controls or logging mechanisms.

title: Data interception during login transmission
description: Parent email and password data transmitted over the network could be intercepted by malicious actors, enabling unauthorized use of authentication credentials.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be adequately encrypted or protected.

title: Identifiability of JWT tokens in transit
description: JWT tokens containing child user type and profile data transmitted in transit could be intercepted and used to identify the child user, especially if tokens are not properly encrypted or if metadata reveals user identity.

title: Linkability of child profile data in transit
description: Child profile data transmitted alongside JWT tokens could be linked with other data sources to create a comprehensive profile of the child, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's identity, preferences, or activities.

title: Unauthorized use of child authentication data
description: Child User (EE2) receiving JWT tokens and profile data could potentially misuse this authentication information for unauthorized access to other systems or services, especially if proper access controls are not enforced.

title: Non-compliance with child data protection regulations
description: Sharing child profile data and authentication tokens may violate regulations like COPPA or GDPR-K which require special protections for children's personal data, including consent mechanisms and data minimization.

title: Linking via Government ID and Personal Attributes
description: The parent (EE1) shares child's government ID, name, DOB, and gender with the profile management process. This combination of attributes can be used to link this child's data to other records, databases, or external systems, potentially creating a comprehensive profile that reveals additional information about the child beyond what was intended to be shared.

title: Direct Identification via Government ID
description: The government ID is a direct identifier that, when combined with name and DOB, can uniquely identify the child. The act of sharing this information at the source creates a risk that the child can be directly identified from the data, potentially leading to unwanted exposure of the child's identity.

title: Data Disclosure in Transit
description: The sensitive child profile data (including government ID) is transmitted from EE1 to P3. If the data flow is not properly secured (e.g., encrypted), the data could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, leading to unauthorized disclosure of the child's personal information.

title: Usurpation via Shared Government ID
description: The parent shares the child's government ID and personal information. This information could be misused by unauthorized actors to impersonate the child in other systems or services, potentially leading to identity theft or unauthorized access to child-related services.

title: Excessive Child Profile Data Collection
description: The process may collect and store more child profile data than strictly necessary for the intended purpose, violating the minimality principle. Child data is particularly sensitive and requires strict adherence to data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Process P3 does not implement data minimization controls when storing child profiles.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard implementation without explicit minimization controls

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Child Profiles
description: The MongoDB data store may lack adequate access controls, allowing unauthorized parties to access stored child profile data. This represents an explicit disclosure risk where data is accessible beyond intended recipients.
assumptions: Data store DS2 does not have role-based access controls or encryption at rest.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard MongoDB deployment without enterprise security hardening

title: Child Identification via Data in Transit
description: Child profile data transmitted from process P3 to data store DS2 may be intercepted, allowing identification of the child. This is particularly concerning given the sensitive nature of child data.
assumptions: Data flow DF7 is not encrypted in transit (e.g., no TLS).
uncertainty_note: Assuming no explicit encryption configuration for this data flow

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data Storage
description: Storing child profile data in MongoDB may violate regulations such as COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) or GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) if proper consent, parental authorization, and data protection measures are not implemented.
assumptions: No documented compliance framework exists for child data handling.
uncertainty_note: Assuming no explicit compliance documentation or controls

title: Child Identifiability in Video Data
description: Child users sharing video content, search queries, likes, and comments may inadvertently reveal personally identifiable information about themselves or others. Video metadata (timestamps, location, device info) combined with content can enable identification of minors.

title: Linkability Across Video Interactions
description: Video search patterns, like/comment behavior, and associated metadata can be used to link a child's activities across different contexts or services, potentially revealing behavioral patterns and preferences.

title: Non-compliance with Child Data Protection Regulations
description: Processing of child user data (video content, comments, search queries) may violate COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child-specific privacy regulations if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, and parental controls are not implemented.
uncertainty_note: Context mentions Nc.2 for improper personal data management; applies to child data processing.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Video Content
description: Video Management Service may store, process, or share video content and associated metadata with third parties (advertisers, analytics providers, law enforcement) without proper authorization or user consent.

title: Child Account Impersonation
description: Child users may share credentials or video content that could be used by others to impersonate them, especially if authentication mechanisms are weak or if children share account access with peers.

title: Identifying information in video metadata
description: Video metadata (timestamps, locations, device IDs, user identifiers) can be used to identify individuals. When stored in transit or at the destination, this metadata may reveal personal information about who was recorded, when, and where.
assumptions: Video metadata contains personally identifiable information that can be extracted and used for identification purposes.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.2 from context as it directly addresses identified information in metadata

title: Unauthorized access to stored video data
description: MongoDB collection DS3 stores video metadata and files. If access controls are insufficient, unauthorized parties may access, view, or download personal video data, leading to data disclosure.
assumptions: The MongoDB collection may not have adequate access controls or encryption at rest.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard MongoDB deployment without additional security context

title: Linkability of video metadata across contexts
description: Video metadata can be used to link different data sources together (e.g., linking video content with user accounts, timestamps, locations, or other system data), potentially creating a comprehensive profile of individuals.
assumptions: Metadata fields contain sufficient information to correlate with other data sources.
uncertainty_note: Standard LINDDUN threat tree node for linkability at flow level

title: Explicit Data Disclosure via Child Search/Watch History Storage
description: The flow stores child search and watch history in MongoDB, constituting an explicit disclosure of personal data by design. This data may contain sensitive information about the child's interests, preferences, and online behavior patterns.

title: Identification Risk from Search/Watch History Metadata
description: The search and watch history data itself may contain identifying information about the child or parent, or metadata that could be used to link this data to other datasets to identify individuals.

title: Linkability of Child Activity Data
description: Search and watch history can be linked with other data sources (e.g., account information, timestamps, device identifiers) to create a comprehensive profile of the child's online behavior, potentially revealing sensitive patterns.

title: Data Disclosure at Storage Destination
description: The MongoDB data store receives and persists child search and watch history. If access controls are insufficient, this stored data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties or third parties.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Child Data
description: The data store may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, allowing entities without proper authorization to view or extract the stored child search and watch history.

title: Video metadata enables user linking
description: Metadata associated with video uploads (timestamps, device info, IP addresses) could be used to link the parent user to specific video content and potentially correlate with other data sources.

title: Video content reveals identifiable information
description: Video content itself may contain personally identifiable information about the parent user or other individuals captured in the video, enabling identification through visual analysis.

title: Unauthorized video data disclosure
description: Video Management Service may store, process, or share video data with unauthorized parties, leading to potential privacy breaches.

title: Improper personal data management
description: Video Management Service may fail to comply with data protection regulations regarding video data retention, access controls, or consent management.

title: Video stream metadata enables child identification
description: Metadata accompanying the video stream (e.g., timestamps, device identifiers, IP addresses) could be used to identify or link the child user to other data systems, compromising their anonymity.

title: Video content enables cross-system linking
description: The video content itself may contain visual or contextual information that could be used to link the child to other data sources, enabling profiling or tracking across systems.

title: Unauthorized access to child video data
description: The child user (EE2) may not have adequate controls to prevent unauthorized access to the received video data, leading to potential disclosure to third parties.

title: Non-compliant video data handling for minors
description: The Video Management Service may not comply with data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) regarding the collection, transmission, and storage of video data involving minors.

title: Explicit disclosure of child browsing data to AI engine
description: Child browsing data is explicitly transferred from MongoDB collection to AI Recommendation Engine for processing. This disclosure may be avoidable if the AI engine's functionality could be achieved with less personal data, or if the disclosure violates minimality principles for children's data.
assumptions: The AI engine processes and potentially stores this child data, creating a disclosure boundary.

title: Linkability of child data in transit
description: Child browsing data in transit between MongoDB and AI engine could be linked to identify specific children or correlate with other data sources, especially if metadata or identifiers are included in the data flow.
assumptions: Data in transit may contain identifiers or metadata that enable linking.

title: Identification of children through AI processing
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may use child browsing data to identify or profile specific children, potentially creating detailed behavioral profiles that could be misused or exposed.
assumptions: AI engine processes data in a way that enables identification or profiling of individual children.

title: Non-compliance with children's data protection regulations
description: Processing children's browsing data may violate GDPR-K or other children's data protection regulations if proper consent, legal basis, or age-appropriate safeguards are not in place.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for children's data apply to this system.

title: Explicit Disclosure of Browsing Data to Third-Party Advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (P4) intentionally shares browsing data with third-party advertisers (EE3) as part of its planned data flow. This represents an explicit data disclosure where personal data is transferred across a system boundary to a known third party. The minimality principle is at risk as the system may share more data than strictly required for the advertising purpose.

title: Linkability via Browsing Data Metadata
description: Browsing data transmitted in flow DF14 may contain metadata (e.g., timestamps, device identifiers, IP addresses) that can be used to link the browsing activity to specific individuals or correlate it with other data sources. This linkability risk exists in the data in transit.

title: Uncontrolled Data Processing by Third-Party Advertisers
description: Third-party advertisers (EE3) receive browsing data and may process, store, or share it in ways that exceed the original purpose of advertising. The destination element's handling of the data creates additional disclosure risks beyond the initial transfer.

title: Identification Risk in Browsing Data Transmission
description: The browsing data transmitted in flow DF14 may contain personally identifiable information or quasi-identifiers that could be used to identify individuals. The data in transit is vulnerable to identification if intercepted or if combined with other available data.

title: Unintended Data Disclosure via File System Storage
description: Government ID images stored in the file system backend/uploads/ may be accessible to unauthorized parties or systems, constituting an unintended disclosure of personal data. The storage location and access controls determine whether this disclosure is avoidable.
assumptions: File system has access controls that may not be properly enforced; storage location may be accessible to internal or external systems beyond intended recipients.

title: Linkability via Image Metadata
description: Metadata embedded in or associated with the government ID images (e.g., timestamps, file names, access logs) could be used to link this data to other data flows or systems, potentially revealing patterns about the authentication service's operations or the individuals whose IDs are stored.
assumptions: Metadata is preserved and accessible; other data flows exist that could be linked to this stored data.

title: Unintentional Information Leakage through File System Artifacts
description: File system artifacts such as access logs, backup copies, or temporary files could unintentionally leak information about the authentication service's operations, the frequency of ID image storage, or which individuals have had their IDs processed.
assumptions: File system generates logs or artifacts that are not properly sanitized or access-controlled.

title: Non-compliance with Data Minimization Principles
description: Storing full government ID images may violate data minimization principles if only certain fields or anonymized versions are strictly required for the authentication service's purpose. The explicit collection and storage of complete ID images may be avoidable.
assumptions: The authentication service's purpose could be achieved with less personal data than full ID images; regulatory requirements may mandate specific data handling.

title: JWT Disclosure via localStorage XSS Vulnerability
description: JWT stored in browser localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript on the page, enabling cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks to exfiltrate authentication tokens. This violates the principle of data minimization and creates unauthorized disclosure risk.
assumptions: Assumes localStorage is not protected by HttpOnly flag and page contains or can be compromised by XSS vectors.

title: JWT Theft Enabling Session Hijacking
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage can be stolen by malicious scripts and used to impersonate users, enabling session hijacking and unauthorized access to protected resources.
assumptions: Assumes JWT contains session claims and localStorage is accessible to third-party scripts.

title: JWT Linkability in Transit
description: JWT data in transit between authentication service and browser could be intercepted, enabling correlation of requests and linking of user sessions across different contexts.
assumptions: Assumes HTTPS is not enforced or is compromised; threat is mitigated if TLS is properly configured.

title: Identifiable JWT Data Sharing
description: Authentication service shares JWT containing user identifiers and claims, making the data inherently identifiable. The act of sharing this data creates identifiability risk.
assumptions: Assumes JWT contains standard claims (sub, iat, exp, etc.) that can identify the user.

title: Child data sharing enables profile linking
description: The process shares child history data with the parent, which could be linked with other data about the child or family members to build a comprehensive profile beyond the intended scope.
assumptions: Child data contains quasi-identifiers or attributes that can be combined with external data sources.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable node for linking threats at source

title: Child identifiable information disclosed to parent
description: The process may share identifiable information about the child with the parent, potentially revealing more than necessary for the intended review purpose.
assumptions: Child data contains personally identifiable information that could be used to identify the child.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a standard identification node; confidence in applicability

title: Data in transit enables linking via metadata
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timestamps, source/destination identifiers) could be used to link this child history data with other data flows or systems.
assumptions: Metadata accompanying the data flow contains linking attributes.
uncertainty_note: L.2.1 is a reasonable node for flow-level linking threats

title: Parent may disclose child data to unauthorized parties
description: The parent user, upon receiving the child history, may share or disclose this sensitive information to third parties without authorization.
assumptions: Parent may not have appropriate safeguards or may share data with others.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a standard disclosure node; assumes parent behavior risk

title: Parent may misuse data to impersonate child
description: The parent could potentially use the child's information to impersonate the child in other systems or contexts.
assumptions: Child data contains sufficient identifying information for impersonation.
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is a reasonable node for usurpation; likelihood is low as this is a legitimate parent-child relationship
